heroHeadline: 10 Days to the World Cup: CDMX Declares Infrastructure Complete — Parque Elevado Opens, Crime at 2022 Lows
heroSubtitle: Mexico City crossed into the final 10-day stretch before the June 11 World Cup opening match at Estadio Ciudad de México with its infrastructure program declared complete: 2,000+ public works finished, the $500M AICM airport renovation wrapped, and 18 free fan zones operational across all 16 alcaldías. Parque Elevado Tlalpan — CDMX's first 1.5-km elevated linear park — inaugurated May 31 as a pedestrian World Cup fan promenade. On the security front, the FGJ-CDMX reported high-impact crimes down 13% in Jan–Apr 2026 vs. 2024 and intentional homicides down 49% since October 2024, with a dedicated World Cup security task force now active. Meanwhile, the CNTE teachers' union continued its Zócalo plantón through the week, Brugada launched 133 human rights strategies ('Juego Limpio, Sociedad Justa') including trafficking prevention, and authorities issued a fraud alert over fake QR codes for neighborhood World Cup access. Metro Line 2 full service resumes June 4.
footerNote: Data sourced from official CDMX government reports (Gobierno CDMX, SSC, SACMEX, SEMOVI, CAMe, CONAGUA, FGJ-CDMX), INEGI, Fiscalía CDMX, Congreso CDMX, NASA, La Jornada, El Universal, Proceso, Milenio, Infobae México, N+, El Financiero, Reuters, AP, Euronews, US News, and institutional analyses from UNAM, IMCO, México Evalúa, and the Institute for Economics and Peace (IEP).
